title: F-4: saturn web admin endpoints are server-side unauthenticated
description: Web-UI admin gate at Web-UI/app.js:1021-1049 is sessionStorage-only; the FastAPI server in saturn/web.py has zero auth dependencies (verified: no Depends(), no Header(), no HTTPBearer use). Endpoints freely callable by any LAN peer: POST /api/services (create), DELETE /api/services/{name}, POST /api/services/{name}/start, POST .../stop, GET/POST /api/admin/config, POST /api/system/tunnel/start (also stop). Attacker can reconfigure the deployment, spawn upstream-binding services, or expose Saturn via cloudflared tunnel. Fix: add a small auth dependency (bearer token from SATURN_ADMIN_TOKEN env or the existing ADMIN_PASSWORD as a session cookie) and apply it to every /api route except /api/health and /v1/* (those have separate F-1 fix). See SECURITY_AUDIT.md F-4.

title: F-1: saturn runner has no auth on /v1/*; binds 0.0.0.0

No rate limit on this endpoint (rate limiter lives in saturn/web.py:252-279 and only covers /api/chat, /api/proxy/chat). Fix: add a required-bearer-token FastAPI dependency on the /v1 router; default bind_host should be 127.0.0.1 unless explicitly opted into 0.0.0.0. See SECURITY_AUDIT.md F-1.

title: Web-UI app.js loaded as classic script but uses ES module syntax
description:
Web-UI/index.html (after hardener commit 896c56d) loads app.js with <script src="app.js"></script>, but Web-UI/app.js:1-3 begins with 'import * as THREE from "three"' (ES module syntax) plus other ES module imports for three/addons/*. The browser parses the file as a classic script and bails on the first import statement, so NONE of the app code runs.

Symptoms (verified via rodney headless against saturn web --port 3030):
- Tab buttons (data-tab=discover/system/chat) work because tab switching is in inline HTML or a separate handler.
- Discover button #discover-btn click does nothing — listener never attached.
- typeof discoverBtn === undefined globally (script never reached its var declarations).
- /api/discover returns the live ollama service correctly. The break is purely in the static page.

Fix options:
1. Change <script src="app.js"></script> to <script type="module" src="app.js"></script> AND add an importmap for 'three' and 'three/addons/*' (the imports app.js makes).
2. Bundle app.js via bun build (Web-UI/server.ts may already do this — check the bun build pipeline).
3. Inline the THREE setup or remove the dependency.

Blocks: demo screenshots in demo/screenshots/. Also blocks any researcher who runs 'saturn web' from a fresh clone.

Repro:
  saturn web --port 3030 &
  saturn ollama &
  open http://127.0.0.1:3030/  # everything past the static markup is dead

title: [role:programmer] Fix arm() timer leak in SettleDetector
description: [role:programmer] arm() in saturn/mdns/settle.py creates a new threading.Timer without canceling the previous one. This causes two bugs: (1) settle fires from the first arm() call, not the last — premature settle on multi-service networks, (2) close() cannot cancel orphaned timers. Fix: cancel self._timer at the start of arm() before creating a new one. description: Found in qj5.14 implementation review. saturn/tests/test_config_honoured.py openrouter_service fixture sets monkeypatch.setenv OPENROUTER_TEST_KEY in the test process, but the saturn_web fixture spawned saturn web as a subprocess earlier with an explicit env dict that does NOT include OPENROUTER_TEST_KEY. title: reclassify_all wiring on /api/admin/config + /api/admin/known-nodes/* (qj5.16.13 §15.4/.5)
description: Gap in qj5.16.13 (commit 150468c). _apply_trust_policy fan-out from POST /api/admin/config updates the module-level _trust_mode/_allowlist globals but does not call reclassify_all() on the live SaturnDiscovery instance. Same for the new /api/admin/known-nodes/attest and /forget POST endpoints. §15.4 explicitly said 'On every successful POST that touches either field, re-classify every record currently in self.services' — and §15.5 said attest 'invokes known_nodes.attest(name, node_id, host) and triggers reclassify_all()'. Effect today: admin flips trust_mode tofu→allowlist (or attests a node) → only future mDNS events pick up the new policy; cached records in _discovered stay stale until the originating server re-announces (mDNS TTL window, default 600s for beacon). Fix: web.py needs a reference to the live SaturnDiscovery (or expose a module-level disc.reclassify_all() that walks all known instances), and call it after each policy mutation. Note: the unit test test_mode_flip_live_update calls reclassify_all manually so the test passes — gap is in the production wiring, not the test invariant.
notes: Closed in commit 8b1e54d. apply_admin_config at saturn/web.py:1417-1426 calls _reclassify_discovered() at end. /api/admin/known-nodes/attest and /forget both call _reclassify_discovered() inline. _reclassify_discovered walks the module-level _discovered cache (the routing source), classifies each entry via _classify_trust, drops rejected ones. Note: spec §15.4 phrased the reclass target as 'self.services' on a SaturnDiscovery instance, but web.py architecture uses _discovered as the persistent cache and creates short-lived SaturnDiscovery instances per /api/discover call — implementation is architecturally correct. Test test_rate_rpm_takes_effect_live confirms live-mutation path. apply_admin_config also clears _rpm_buckets/_tpm_buckets/_ip_semaphores on rate-config change — bonus over §15.4 contract.

title: Wire TrustRebindError into saturn/web.py:_resolve (qj5.16.13 §15.3)
description: Gap found in qj5.16.13 review (commit 150468c). The TrustRebindError class is defined in saturn/discovery.py but is never raised. §15.3 of SECURITY_AUDIT.md specified the resolver should detect 'zero selectable candidates AND at least one rebind-rejected' and raise the structured 403 with remediation field, so the chat UI can show a non-dismissable banner with admin-attest instructions. As shipped, a hijack attempt produces a generic 404 'Service not found' which is indistinguishable from a stopped service. Fix: in saturn/web.py:_resolve (line 562), when the configured service is not in _discovered, check known_nodes.load()['rejected'] for a recent rejection of ; if found, raise HTTPException(403, detail={...}) per §15.3's exact shape. Required before qj5.16.13 commit-3 UI work — frontend banner needs the 403 to render against.
notes: Closed in commit 8b1e54d. /api/admin/_resolve at saturn/web.py:585-598 raises HTTPException(403, detail={...}) with all six required fields per §15.3 (error/service/expected_prefix/seen_prefix/seen_host/remediation). Implementation chose to raise HTTPException directly rather than the named TrustRebindError class (which now becomes dead code in saturn/discovery.py:28-37 — see follow-up Saturn-qj5.16.13.4). Wire result is identical to the spec; clients see the same JSON shape. Tests test_resolve_raises_403_when_rejection_recorded + test_resolve_403_takes_precedence_over_404 confirm the 403 wins over the 404 path.

title: Beacon sleep-transition unregister + power-mgmt opt-in (qj5.16/§16)
description: Implementer follow-up to SECURITY_AUDIT.md §16. Two changes in run_beacon (saturn/runner.py): (a) Register for platform sleep notifications (NSWorkspaceWillSleep on macOS via pyobjc or helper; D-Bus PrepareForSleep on linux deferred until needed). On sleep: beacon.unregister(). On wake: credential_manager.create() then beacon.re_register() — so freshly-advertised TXT carries a fully-fresh key, not a ragged-tail credential. (b) On beacon start, detect laptop power state; offer to hold an IOPMAssertion (macOS) / systemd-inhibit session (linux) for run_beacon lifetime, with a [Y] keep awake / [n] allow sleep prompt. Decline path logs a single warning citing §16. Ship in same PR as beacon.max_budget_usd plumbing from §7.5 — both touch run_beacon.
notes: Pre-spec drafted in PRE_SPECS_B3.md §17.E. Same nine-section shape as §15. KeepAwake (caffeinate -i -w / systemd-inhibit) + SleepWatcher (NSWorkspace / D-Bus PrepareForSleep) decoupled into saturn/mdns/sleep.py. run_beacon integration in three seams (acquire keep-awake, watcher when declined, rotation-loop hardening with monotonic-jump heuristic for unwitnessed sleep). BeaconConfig adds keep_awake / keep_awake_decided / sleep_handling. CLI prompt + Configure-page row for first-run UX. Six tests covering KeepAwake lifecycle, SleepWatcher event ordering, beacon-unregisters-on-sleep + re-mints-on-wake, monotonic-jump fallback, declined-watcher warning, CLI prompt persistence. Co-landable with §7.5 beacon budget plumbing — both touch run_beacon. Optional deps pyobjc-framework-Cocoa + jeepney via [project.optional-dependencies] beacon in pyproject.toml; non-beacon installs stay clean.

title: F-3 sub: /api/usage* user_id query bypasses client identity
description: Uncovered while tracing F-3 (see SECURITY_AUDIT.md §8.5). saturn/web.py:1246 (/api/usage) and :1275 (/api/usage/history) accept user_id as a Query() param that completely overrides _client_ip(). On a /24 LAN an attacker iterates 254 IPs and reads each peer's daily token totals + N-day history. Fix: require admin_token_env on both routes (CONFIG_FIELDS A.5 auth matrix); when not authenticated, ignore user_id and serve only the caller's own row.
notes: Closed in SECURITY_AUDIT.md §9. Defect at saturn/web.py:1246 and :1275: 'user_id or _client_ip(request)' lets caller-supplied query parameter override identity entirely. Schema (saturn/web.py:282-316) holds aggregate counts only — no chat content — so severity is MEDIUM disclosure of per-peer daily token totals + N-day history (privacy / presence signal across the LAN), would escalate to HIGH if schema ever gains per-model or per-conversation fields. Fix: Depends(require_admin) on both GET routes per CONFIG_FIELDS A.5 matrix; /api/usage/report stays self-report-only keyed by _client_ip post-§8 trust gate. Tests in §9.6, posture prose in §9.7.

Headline: OpenRouter sub-key payload passes no spending cap (saturn/providers/openrouter.py:12-17), DeepInfra revoke is no-op, default expiration_interval=600 > rotation_interval*1.5=450 violates the freshness invariant. title: F-3: X-Forwarded-For trusted unconditionally — rate-limit bypass
description: saturn/web.py:245-249 _client_ip() returns the first comma-split value of X-Forwarded-For if present, with no allowlist of trusted proxies. Any LAN attacker rotates the header per request and gets unlimited requests-per-minute and tokens-per-minute against /api/chat. Fix: only honor XFF when the immediate peer is in a configured trusted_proxies list (default empty); otherwise use request.client.host. See SECURITY_AUDIT.md F-3.
notes: F-3 traced and documented in SECURITY_AUDIT.md §8. Three independent bugs in saturn/web.py:245-249: (1) no trust gate, (2) takes leftmost XFF entry — the most-attacker-controlled byte — instead of rightmost, (3) ignores Forwarded/X-Real-IP. Seven callsites; primary impact is rate-limit bypass on /api/proxy/chat, /api/chat, /api/system/chat. Discovered companion bug filed as Saturn-qj5.16.10 (user_id query bypass on /api/usage*). Drop-in _client_ip replacement provided in §8.4 aligned with CONFIG_FIELDS A.3 trusted_proxies. Posture-ready prose in §8.7 for docs queue.

title: Fix model fallback in Brutus sending invalid 'default' to backends
description: When a user sends a message without selecting a model via /model, user_models.get() returns None. In _stream_from(), the fallback logic is: effective_model = model or (service.models[0] if service.models else 'default'). Since service.models is always empty for custom module servers, this resolves to the string 'default'. The claude server MODEL_MAP only contains claude-code-opus, claude-code-sonnet, claude-code-haiku. It returns HTTP 400 'Unknown model: default'. This is the direct cause of 'All backends failed to respond.' Trace: bot.py:444 (None) -> bot.py:168 ('default') -> claude.py:64-66 (400).

title: Fix SaturnAdvertiser unregister() destroying backend on re-registration
description: In runner.py lifespan handler, unregister() calls close() which kills the Bonjour event loop threads irreversibly. The subsequent register() call operates on a dead backend, triggering a Bonjour name conflict. The conflict callback spawns a background thread to re-register with a new name, resulting in duplicate mDNS entries. Trace: run_service() -> advertiser.register() [first], then lifespan -> advertiser.unregister() -> backend.close() [kills threads] -> advertiser.register() [dead backend, triggers conflict] -> _reregister() on background thread [creates second entry]. The withdraw() vs close() distinction exists in bonjour.py but unregister() calls both.

description:
Found in 70f7beb review against §17.A.5 commit-2. saturn/web.py:admin_configure_route iterates AdminConfig.model_fields and skips bool values via 'if isinstance(v, bool): continue'; the regex pattern matches `<input...id="ac-FIELD"` which does NOT match `<select>`. Effect: three fields are NEVER pre-filled at server-render time:

- ac-require_auth_on_v1 (checkbox)
- ac-redact_proxy_keys_in_logs (checkbox)
- ac-trust_mode (select)

app.js's loadAdminConfigure() AJAX repairs within 500ms via `el.checked = !!v` / `el.value = ...`, but until that fires the SSR'd page shows the wrong default — checkboxes unchecked, trust_mode showing 'tofu' even when admin set it to 'allowlist'. Bounded for users who tolerate a half-second visual flicker, but the v2 test test_section_values_populate_current_config only checks rate_rpm (a numeric input) so the gap silently passes CI.

Fix: add a substitution that adds `selected` attribute to the matching `<option>` for select fields, and a substitution that adds `checked` attribute to `<input type="checkbox">` for booleans. P2 — visible to admins on bookmark-load.

title: Field-def drift guard: meta-test for AdminConfig.model_fields ↔ AC_FIELDS parity
description: Found in 70f7beb review. After Option-A collapse there are still TWO independent definitions of the 22-field schema: (1) saturn/web.py AdminConfig.model_fields (Pydantic, server source-of-truth), (2) Web-UI/app.js AC_FIELDS (client, with type tags). They can drift in two directions: (a) Field added to AdminConfig but not AC_FIELDS → UI silently misses the field on load+save; server is happy. Worst kind of drift — silent. (b) Field in AC_FIELDS but not AdminConfig → POST returns 422 because AdminConfig has extra='forbid'. Loud failure; less bad. The existing meta-test test_every_admin_config_field_has_roundtrip_row enforces (1) ↔ test ROUNDTRIP_TABLE. An analogous UI-side meta-test should enforce (1) ↔ AC_FIELDS: import saturn.web.AdminConfig, read Web-UI/app.js as text, regex-extract AC_FIELDS keys, assert symmetric difference is empty. ~15 lines of pytest. P2 — guards against the drift the snapshot already flagged.

title: Live-propagation tests cover only rate_rpm (qj5.13 §17.A.4.3 partial)

None of these have a live-propagation test as shipped. Implementation in apply_admin_config does mutate them (clears _rpm_buckets/_tpm_buckets/_ip_semaphores and calls _apply_trust_policy + _reclassify_discovered), but there is no should-not-regress test asserting the mutation actually changes downstream behaviour without restart. Suggested: parametrise live-propagation test over the full set, with one assertion shape per field (rate-bucket → 429, public_routes flip → auth-gate behaviour, trust_mode → resolved-service identity). Counterpart: the spec also said A.3 TLS paths + bind_host are restart-only and 'response body says so' — no test asserts that signal either. P2 because the implementation appears correct; gap is in coverage.

title: bind_host validator vs CLI-default disagreement (qj5.14 vs CONFIG_FIELDS A.3)
description: Found in qj5.14 review. C.1.4 boot validator (saturn/boot_validators.py:55-60 + duplicate at saturn/web.py:1573) reads os.environ SATURN_BIND_HOST defaulting to '127.0.0.1'. Actual uvicorn bind defaults to '0.0.0.0' (saturn/__main__.py:92, saturn/web.py:1650). Two consequences: (i) admin runs python3 -m saturn web with default flags + admin/runner tokens set; validator sees 'bind=127.0.0.1' (greens up) but uvicorn binds 0.0.0.0 — the LAN-exposure-requires-auth check is bypassed because the validator's view of bind_host disagrees with reality; tokens are still required by C.1.2/C.1.3 so security still holds, but the C.1.4 invariant is structurally false. (ii) CONFIG_FIELDS A.3 specified bind_host default '127.0.0.1' (admin opts into LAN); the shipping CLI default is still '0.0.0.0' — schema not honoured. Fix: read bind_host from admin_config.json first (canonical source per A.3), env override second; flip saturn/__main__.py:92 + saturn/web.py:1650 default to '127.0.0.1'.

title: SettleDetector integration in TOFU pin (qj5.16.13 §15.2.b race)
description: Minor race noted in qj5.16.13 review. §15.2.b said 'On first observation of (name, node_id) with trust=first_seen: promote to pinned after the SettleDetector reports steady state (avoids pinning on a transient mDNS glitch).' Implementation in saturn/discovery.py:_add pins immediately. Race: an attacker who times their priority-0 advertisement to land before the honest server during discovery startup can grab the TOFU pin on a fresh client install. Bounded — only matters at first-ever discovery against a never-seen-before service name. Mitigation: defer the known_nodes.pin() call until SettleDetector signals quiet, or apply only if the same (name, node_id) pair has been seen ≥2 times within the settle window. (b) ACME mode — vendored lego/acme.sh fetches Let's Encrypt cert when admin owns a public DNS name; right fit for tunneled/hosted scenarios. Not security plumbing — meaningful product work that decides whether Saturn's TLS story is actually adoptable. Defer until §13.5 steps 1-3 land.

title: F-8: mDNS service identity is unauthenticated — priority hijack
description: Any LAN peer can register a _saturn._tcp.local. service with priority=1 and steal traffic from clients that pick lowest-priority. mDNS itself has no signing. Mitigations to consider: (a) clients prefer node_id seen previously (TOFU); (b) admin config holds an allowlist of expected node_ids; (c) per-deployment shared HMAC in TXT that clients verify before trusting api_base. See SECURITY_AUDIT.md F-8.
notes: F-8 closed in SECURITY_AUDIT.md §14. mDNS announce/resolve flow traced; priority=0 attacker wins get_best_service() unconditionally. Demonstrated TLS alone (§13) does NOT close F-8 because the attacker controls api_base in the TXT — TLS authenticates a chosen endpoint, not the choice of endpoint. Three-layer mitigation: (1) TOFU on node_id, recommended near-term; (2) admin allowlist via new trusted_node_ids/trust_mode CONFIG_FIELDS rows; (3) signed TXT records, deferred. §14.5 lists deployment-time mitigations (api_base pinning, VLAN segmentation). §14.6 closes the structural-audit bucket with a compounding-finding inventory. SETTLE DETECTION RESEARCH — Saturn-6pj.1

## Current discover() settle logic (saturn/discovery.py:205-231)

`discover(timeout=8.0, settle_time=1.0)` uses a polling loop:
1. Creates SaturnDiscovery with on_change callback
2. Callback sets `last_discovery_time[0] = time.time()` on each 'added' event
3. Loop polls every 0.25s via `service_event.wait(timeout=0.25)`
4. After first service found, checks `time.time() - last_discovery_time[0] >= settle_time`
5. If no new service for settle_time seconds, breaks out
6. Hard timeout at `timeout` seconds if settle never triggers

This is a pure heuristic — no protocol signal. On congested networks it may return early (missing peers); on empty networks it waits the full 8s timeout.

## Callers of discover() with settle_time

- discover() default: timeout=8.0, settle_time=1.0
- runner.py:70 is_service_running(): timeout=3.0, settle_time=0.5
- SaturnAdvertiser._find_available_priority(): timeout=2.0, settle_time=0.5
- saturn-mcp/server.py: multiple calls with timeout=5.0, settle_time=1.0
- ralph tests: timeout=0.5/0.3/4.0, settle_time=0.1/1.0

## time.sleep() in tests (all heuristic waits for mDNS propagation)

test_discovery.py — 10 sleeps:
  - 7x time.sleep(2.5) — standard wait after registering/removing services
  - 2x time.sleep(3) — longer wait for multi-service or advertiser roundtrip tests
  - Pattern: register service, sleep(2.5-3), then assert services found

test_integration.py — 3 sleeps:
  - 3x time.sleep(3) — same pattern as discovery tests

## What the v2 spec says should replace this

1. Avahi: `AllForNow` D-Bus signal fires when cache sweep complete → immediate settle
2. Bonjour: absence of `kDNSServiceFlagsMoreComing` flag in browse callback → batch complete
3. Userspace (zeroconf fallback): Timer(0.5s) after browser construction (RFC §6: responses arrive within 300ms)
4. New discover() calls backend.wait_for_settle(timeout) instead of polling loop
5. Tests replace time.sleep() with wait_for_settle() → target <1s per test vs current 2.5-3s

## _find_available_priority() issue (discovery.py:402-419)

Called during EVERY SaturnAdvertiser.register(). Runs a full discover(timeout=2.0) scan just to avoid priority collisions. The spec says remove this entirely — priority is a soft preference, duplicates are fine. This adds 2s to every service startup.

BUG 1 (arm() timer leak): arm() creates a new threading.Timer without canceling the previous one. When multiple services are discovered, settle fires from the FIRST arm() call, not the LAST. This means on networks where services arrive over 500ms+, discover() settles prematurely and misses late-arriving services. Test: test_arm_resets_timer_on_subsequent_calls — FAILS.

BUG 2 (close() orphaned timers): close() only cancels self._timer (the last reference). If arm() was called multiple times, earlier timers are orphaned and still fire, setting the event after close(). Test: test_close_cancels_orphaned_timers — FAILS.

FIX: arm() must cancel self._timer before creating a new one. This fixes both bugs — no orphaned timers means close() only needs to cancel self._timer.
